model_annotation:
The line plot illustrates the average accuracy (ACC) percentages of various methods as a function of Co-occurrence Number. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)" and expressed as a percentage of accuracy, ranges from 40 to 65%. The plot includes seven lines representing different methods: "Base" with a black solid line and circle markers, "MEND" with a brown solid line and diamond markers, "FT" with a blue solid line and triangle markers, "IKE" with a red solid line and inverted triangle markers, "ROME" with a green solid line and square markers, and one more method with unspecified label shown by a pink diamond.

The "ROME" method, represented by green squares, starts with the highest accuracy at the initiating Co-occurrence Number and exhibits a steady increase as the count rises. The "Base" method, shown in black, maintains the lowest accuracy range above 40% across all Co-occurrence Numbers. The remaining methods demonstrate varying degrees of accuracy growth. The "FT" method (blue triangles) and "IKE" method (red inverted triangles) have similar trends, with accuracy improving modestly over the Co-occurrence Number. The "MEND" method (brown diamonds) has a moderate increase, ending with higher accuracy compared to the "Base" but lower than the "ROME" method at the highest Co-occurrence Number. The accuracy of the method with unspecified labels (pink diamonds) starts at approximately 45% at the Co-occurrence Number of 10^0 and shows a steep increase, ending with the highest accuracy at 10^3 among all methods depicted.
